standards.title: Energy and thermodynamics
standards.description: Students explain energy forms and the laws that govern energy in living systems.
iCan: I can tell kinetic energy (motion, including heat) from potential energy (stored, including chemical energy in bonds)
I can define metabolism and tell anabolic pathways (build and store) from catabolic pathways (break down and release)
I can state the first law of thermodynamics (energy is conserved, not created or destroyed)
I can state the second law (entropy increases, some energy is lost as heat) and explain why cells need a constant energy input

reading.sectionTitle: Cells and the Flow of Energy

standards.title: Free energy and spontaneity
standards.description: Students use free energy to predict whether a reaction proceeds on its own.
iCan: I can define free energy (G) and change in free energy (delta G)
I can tell exergonic reactions (release energy, negative delta G, spontaneous) from endergonic reactions (absorb energy, positive delta G)
I can explain why spontaneous does not mean fast
I can explain that reactions run toward equilibrium, and why a living cell avoids equilibrium

standards.title: ATP and energy coupling
standards.description: Students explain how ATP stores and delivers energy for cellular work.
iCan: I can describe the parts of ATP: adenine, ribose, and three phosphate groups
I can explain that hydrolysis of ATP's last phosphate bond releases usable energy, forming ADP plus phosphate
I can explain energy coupling: how ATP hydrolysis drives reactions and cellular work
I can describe the ATP cycle: how ATP is recharged from ADP plus phosphate using energy from catabolism

standards.title: Enzymes
standards.description: Students explain how an enzyme's structure lets it speed up reactions, and what changes its rate.
iCan: I can define an enzyme as a biological catalyst that speeds a reaction without being used up
I can explain that enzymes work by lowering activation energy, not by changing delta G
I can explain the active site, substrate specificity, and induced fit
I can explain how temperature, pH, and concentration change the rate, including an optimum and denaturation

exam.examItems: MC Q8, Q9; SA 16; Part 3 CER; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Enzyme regulation
standards.description: Students explain how cells control enzyme activity.
iCan: I can tell a competitive inhibitor from a noncompetitive (allosteric) inhibitor
I can explain allosteric regulation: how a molecule at a regulatory site can turn an enzyme on or off
I can explain feedback inhibition: how a pathway's end product shuts down an earlier enzyme
I can explain that many enzymes need cofactors (inorganic) or coenzymes (organic, like vitamins)
